page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression single-threaded tests all ranking in the top 10%. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, small-block memory bandwidth, and write memory bandwidth fall into the average tier. General computing benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and Passmark CPU tests, also perform within the average range.

The shared CPU allocation model represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, exclusive CPU utilization, though the underlying AMD EPYC architecture mitigates this with robust single-core execution. Lacking local storage, this server relies on external storage volumes. Given the 128.0 GB memory capacity and strong single-threaded performance, this configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, database operations, and lightweight text generation or LLM inference tasks.
